chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Saif ibn Amirah and Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah and Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Regarding a woman who has a husband who is a slave, and her master dies and she inherits him, he said: 'There is no marriage bond between them.'
ai.seo_question: Does a female slave inherit her master's husband as a spouse if he dies?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that when a female slave inherits her master upon his death, the resulting ownership does not constitute a new marriage contract (*nikah*), preserving the distinct legal nature of inheritance versus matrimony. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between the bond of *milk al-yamin* (ownership) and *nikah*, ensuring that the transition from slave-owner to heir does not automatically alter marital status without explicit contractual intent. It underscores the precision of Shia legal theory in separating property rights from personal status laws.
